title: Israeli strike on al-Mawasi targets Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif
body:
On 13 July 2024, Israeli aircraft struck a building in al-Mawasi, near Khan Younis in southern Gaza, an area that Israel had designated a humanitarian zone for displaced persons. The Israeli military said the target was Mohammed Deif, who led the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades, the military wing of Hamas in Gaza, and had evaded Israeli attempts to kill or capture him for more than two decades. The Gaza Ministry of Health reported at least 90 dead and 300 wounded in the attack.

About two and a half weeks later, on 1 August 2024, the IDF confirmed Deif's death. It said intelligence indicated that Deif and Rafa Salama, his second in command and head of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, had left an underground tunnel and entered an aboveground complex owned by Salama. After confirming Deif's identity, two jets fired missiles at the building. Salama's death was confirmed within hours of the strike. The IDF released a short video of the strike.

Hamas did not immediately respond to requests for comment when the IDF made its announcement. The International Criminal Court nevertheless issued a warrant for Deif on 21 November 2024, saying it could not determine whether he was dead or alive.
